question.:question/problem:
Use the substitution $u=x^{2}$. Which integral is obtained?

$$
\int 3 x \csc^{2}{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=x^{2}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2 x.
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 3 x \csc^{2}{\left(x^{2} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \csc^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed integral is

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \csc^{2}{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$
